title: Ephemeral metric glitches and threshold resilience notes
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from the late-Nov oncall where we observed several short-lived metric dropouts that caused an SLO burn spike and a flurry of high-priority pages. This doc collects the timeline, immediate mitigations we used during the incident, hypotheses we want to validate, and a short runbook draft for 'threshold resilience' to reduce noisy pages from transient signal gaps.

Why this matters:
- Multiple team members paged despite the underlying user-visible error rate being low (customer-facing latency/inference errors did not match SLO burn).
- Short-window SLOs (1m/5m) saw big % jumps driven by gaps in a few core histograms and a missing heartbeat metric for the request router.
- We need to avoid human time wasted chasing symptoms from flaky telemetry.

Timeline (rough):
- 2024-11-09 03:14 UTC: Alert flood starts - ~50 pages in 10 minutes from SLO burn on model-generation-route-1m-slo
- 03:15 UTC: Ops triage - dashboards show spike in "slo_burn_rate_1m" but request_error_rate panels flat; heatmap shows metric gaps for "request_latency_histogram_bucket" across 3 hosts
- 03:18 UTC: Hotfix - temporarily relaxed 1m SLO alert to 10% margin via alert mute for 8 minutes to stop paging while investigating
- 03:22 UTC: Identified that agent exporter on instance pool-a had CPU starve leading to stalled histogram flushes (node-level CPU contention with nightly batch job)
- 03:29 UTC: Restarted exporter process on 3 hosts; monitored metrics returning to normal by 03:34 UTC
- 03:40 UTC: Re-enabled alert with buffer and added temp suppressor for transient gaps

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Short alert mute + escalation to SRE leads so we could focus on root cause without repeated wakeups.
- Restarted metric exporter and rotated batch job cadence on the affected host group.
- Adjusted alerting rule to require error_count > 0 and metadata heartbeat present for 2 consecutive windows before firing (see runbook change proposals).

Root-cause hypotheses (to validate):
1) Telemetry thin spots: exporter process (python-based) got <10% CPU share due to overlapping batch jobs causing histogram aggregations to miss flush deadlines.
2) Metric ingestion path sensitivity: our Prometheus push-proxy has transient queue backpressure thresholds that drop buckets when host export bursts saturate IO.
3) Alert rule sensitivity: 1m SLO windows combined with hard thresholds are too brittle for multi-second telemetry gaps.
4) Crash-only instrumentation in some libraries meaning a single exporter failure zeros out the histogram series instead of reverting to no-data semantics.

PromQL checks to run (examples):
- Check heartbeat: up{job="request-router", region="us-west-2"} == 1
- Gap detection: increase(count_over_time(request_latency_bucket[10m]), 1) OR absent(request_latency_bucket[5m])
- Compare SLO driver vs user-visible errors: rate(request_errors_total[1m]) and slo_burn_rate_1m

Proposed runbook change: "Threshold resilience for short-window SLOs" (draft steps)
- Pre-conditions: alerts for 1m SLOs must include a telemetry-health guard: a dedicated "telemetry_heartbeat" metric for each cluster/zone.
- Firing conditions: require both slo_burn_rate_1m > X AND telemetry_heartbeat == 1 for at least 2 consecutive windows, otherwise mark as "telemetry-suspect" and open low-priority incident.
- Auto-mitigations: when telemetry-suspect detected, mute page routing for 10 minutes and create an SRE-assigned task to validate exporters.
- Post-incident: if telemetry-suspect persists > 20m, escalate to infra on-call for potential ingestion backpressure or disk/IO issues.
- Dashboarding: add a "presence/freshness" ribbon for all histogram-based metrics so that each series shows last-seen timestamp and a binary fresh/stale state.

Checklist for oncall triage (quick, to reduce churn):
- Does the user-visible error/latency dashboard show matching signal? If no, mark telemetry-suspect.
- Check exporter and heartbeat metrics for the hosts in the affected pool.
- Run a tail on exporter logs for TTL/flush errors and OOMs.
- Validate Prometheus ingestion queues and scrape duration percentiles.
- If exporters are down, rotate and restart, then watch metric reappearance for 2 cycles before unmuting alerts.

Follow-up action items (owners):
- Marcus Liu: prototype heartbeat metric that is emitted from sidecar and is independent of histogram flush (due 2024-11-22).
- Riley Gomez: short doc on migration of heavy nightly batch jobs off critical exporter hosts; propose new job-shard schedule (due 2024-12-02).
- Noah Carter: create alert rule PR to implement telemetry-suspect gating for 1m SLOs and add binary freshness ribbon to dashboards (PR by 2024-11-30).
- Asha Patel: run a 2-week experiment to widen 1m alert windows for low-traffic routes to 2m and compare pager frequency (experiment start 2024-11-18).

Longer term engineering asks:
- Improve exporter resilience: move costly histogram aggregation to a native goroutine that yields under CPU pressure (reduce Python process sensitivity).
- Add ingestion backpressure telemetry: expose queue depth, enqueue/drop counts on push-proxy and ingestion layer.
- Consider moving critical SLOs to multi-signal evaluation (combine client-side error signal + server SLO proxy) so noisy telemetry paths alone don't generate pages.

Retrospective notes (what went well / could be better):
- Went well: quick identification of metric gaps vs real user errors; team coordination and temporary mute prevented additional wakeups.
- Could be better: we didn't have a dedicated telemetry-health signal per cluster; runbook steps for telemetry-suspect gating were not present before this incident.

Open questions for next retro:
- Should we standardize a "telemetry-health" naming and label set across teams to make alert gating generic?
- What is the right default for short-window SLO gating (2m? require 2 consecutive fire windows?).
- How much noise reduction is acceptable vs potential detection latency cost? (we should model trade-offs).

Notes to self / oncall tips: quick commands to run during a page:
- kubectl -n telemetry logs -l app=exporter --tail=200 | egrep -i "flush|timeout|drop|oom"
- curl prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=absent_over_time(request_latency_bucket[5m])
- watch -n5 'sum(rate(scrape_duration_seconds_count[1m])) by (instance)'
